newsitem.title: INDIA: India Reliance shr registrar to appeal suspension.
newsitem.headline: India Reliance shr registrar to appeal suspension.

text.p: The share registrar and transfer agent for Reliance Industries Ltd said on Wednesday it will file an appeal against its suspension by the market regulator.

Reliance Consultancy Services (RCS), the sole share registrar and transfer agent for the Reliance group, said it received an order from the Securities and Exchange Board of India (SEBI) suspending it for six months.
"RCS will prefer an appeal against the said order before the Ministry of Finance," a company spokesman said in a statement.
SEBI chief D.R. Mehta earlier told reporters on Wednesday he decided to suspend RCS from February 1, 1997 to July 31, 1997 for improper share swaps.

"I'm convinced that RCS have failed to maintain records for transactions ....that RCS have not conducted their activities in a manner which is fair, diligent and with care, skill and with integrity," he said.
Mehta said RCS has been given time uptil January 31, 1997 to make alternate arrangements for shareholders of the Reliance group.
Reliance Industries said in a separate statement that shareholders "would not be put to any inconvenience as a result of the said order".
The petrochemicals giant has 2.6 million shareholders.
"Reliance Industries Ltd (RIL) has already taken a series of initiatives in the best interests of its investors," the statement said.

"RIL has taken the lead in opting into the depository mechanism being launched ... in the first week of November 1996," it said. "Reliance Petroleum Ltd will be moving into the depository mechanism in the second phase of operations in 1997.
